mutations.name: a disabled rule still orders the repo
kills: the merge-order guard reads nothing at all under the shipped rule file, which leaves every repo unordered
a merge step behind a merge-order reservation merges at once under the shipped rule file, as it did before merge order existed

mutations.name: a stacked PR is ordered too
kills: the merge-order guard never orders a disabled repo, the Version Packages branch, a stacked PR or an unregistered PR

mutations.name: a merged or closed reserving PR keeps blocking
kills: the merge-order guard stops holding once the reserving PR has merged or closed
a merge step behind a merge-order reservation waits in the merge step and answers held, merging nothing, while an overlapping reservation is live

mutations.name: unread paths overlap nothing
mutations.find: if (read.unread !== undefined) return { paths: [], unread: true };
kills: the merge-order guard holds a PR whose changed paths cannot be read until the reservation passes its TTL
